newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Finmin says lev drop highly speculative.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Finmin says lev drop highly speculative.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev recovered to 1,560-1,590 per dollar at midday from the morning's fall to 1,600-1,630 after Saturday's poll as interim Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said the drop was highly speculative.

"The fall was due to speculation that the dollar will sharply rise after the poll. However, this is not justified as Bulgaria has secured enough foreign funding to service its foreign debt payments this year", Gavriiski told reporters.
The lev closed at 1,535-1,545 on Friday.
It was not true that the lev has been kept artificially stable until the parliamentary elections, Gavriiski said.
"I see no reason for a further lev drop other than unjustified talk that the lev has been stabilised through administrative measures just to win the election," Gavriiski said.
Speculative pressure on the lev was expected to be short lived as dollar bidders withdrew from the market around midday considering levels around 1,600-1,630 as too low for the lev, traders said.
The Union of Democratic Forces won 52 percent of the votes cast in Saturday's election and was expected to carry on painful economic reforms launched by the interim cabinet.

Dealers said some foreign investors were willing to sell dollars and purchase government securities despite a cut in the central bank main interest rate to 8.03 percent from 14.15 percent, which came into force today.
"Foreign investors seem confident that the new government will continue the interim cabinet's reformist policy, which encourages them to invest in domestic debt," another dealer said.

Bulgaria's interim government, in office since mid-February has won pledges of some $1.2 billion from international lenders, including a $657 million funding package from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Under an agreement with the IMF Bulgaria is expected to introduce in June a restrictive fixed exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board system, to stabilise its economy.

The system would require levs in circulation to be fully matched by foreign exchange reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the central bank and the Finance ministry and preventing the printing of money.

The lev has been stable between 1,500 and 1,600 per dollar since the beginning of March, up from all-time lows of 2,900-3,200 it hit amid political instability in early February before the interim cabinet took office.

Most foreign investors in local debt have made yield projections at an exchange rate of around 2,000 levs per dollar at the introduction of the currency board which explained their ongoing interest in Bulgarian government paper, traders said.
Bulgaria has to pay around $650 million on foreign debt in the remaining three quarters, central bank figures showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
